# Jubilees Chapter 13 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 13:17 — Number of Abram's fighters: "eighteen and three hundred" vs. "three hundred and eighteen"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "eighteen and three hundred" | Follows Ge'ez word order |
| LOGOS | "three hundred and eighteen" | Standard English number order |
| PNEUMA | "three hundred and eighteen men" | Same as LOGOS, adds "men" |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. English number convention puts the larger number first. EMET's "eighteen and three hundred" follows Semitic number syntax but is non-standard in English.

---

## 13:20 — "I raise my hand" vs. "I lift up mine hand"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I lift up mine hand to the LORD God Most High" | Archaic literal |
| LOGOS | "I raise my hand to the LORD God Most High" | Modern formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "I swear by the LORD God Most High" | Paraphrases the gesture |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "I raise my hand" preserves the oath-gesture from the Ge'ez while being natural in English. PNEUMA's "I swear by" loses the physical gesture which is present in the source. EMET's "mine hand" is archaic.

---

## 13:22 — "chief of the spoils" vs. "prime spoils"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a tithe of all the chief of the spoils" | "Chief" as adjective |
| LOGOS | "a tithe of all the chief of the spoils" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "a tenth of all the prime spoils" | "Prime" for "chief of" |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET. "The chief of the spoils" = the first/best portion of the spoils — a technical term for the tithe offering. "Prime spoils" (PNEUMA) is natural but loses the hierarchical designation.

---

## 13:26 — "five weeks of years" — render or convert?

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "five weeks of years" | Jubilees calendrical unit |
| LOGOS | "five weeks of years" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "thirty-five years" in text; "five weeks of years" in notes | Converts to years for clarity |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Five weeks of years" is the Jubilees expression. Converting to "thirty-five years" (PNEUMA) is clarifying but removes the calendrical vocabulary of the text.

---

## 13:27 — "maidservant" vs. "handmaid"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "handmaid" | Traditional KJV rendering |
| LOGOS | "maidservant" | Modern formal |
| PNEUMA | "maidservant" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS "maidservant." Both are valid; "maidservant" is more transparent in modern English. "Handmaid" (EMET) is accurate but slightly archaic.

---

**Total disagreements: 5**
